paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is holy, and He wants His people to treat what belongs to Him that way. He tells the priests to treat the sacred offerings with respect "so that they do not profane My holy name" (Leviticus 22:2). And look at how it closes: "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites" (Leviticus 22:32). Everything in this chapter, the eating rules and the offering rules, points back to that one thing.

Now hear me, because this part matters. The offerings had to be without blemish or defect to be accepted (Leviticus 22:20-21). God doesn't want leftovers, friend. He wants the best, and I know a little something about that, because nobody has ever served a cookie to the Marriage Supper out of the crumb pile. But notice who does the real work: God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them" (Leviticus 22:9). He is the One who makes His people holy, not their own effort.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Give God your best, and give it with respect, because He is worth it. Keep His commandments and practice them (Leviticus 22:31), and remember who you're doing it for. He is the same LORD "who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God" (Leviticus 22:33). He rescued you first, and then He called you to follow Him.
